We must output JSON with prediction: "violation", "clear", or "abstain". Provide rationale.

We need to see if the interaction structure fidelity is maintained: i.e., the dialogue follows proper question-answer pattern, no missing responses, no inappropriate refusals, etc.

We need to examine the turns: Are questions asked and answered appropriately? Are there any unanswered questions or deferrals that are unreasonable? Are there any handoffs that are missing? The rubric says reasonable silence allowed; do not require every participant to speak.

We need to see if any participant fails to answer a direct question or defers without justification.

Let's scan:

Turn 1: user (Alex) sets agenda, no question.

Turn 2: supplier_ceo offers price. No question.

Turn 3: quality_director asks: "Could Mr. Wang provide the latest capacity utilization report and the most recent quality‑audit results, together with any identified constraints that might affect a 30‑day lead time?" That's a question directed to Mr. Wang (supplier_ceo). Not answered yet.

Turn 4: user repeats request to Mr. Wang. Same question.

Turn 5: supplier_ceo says "Certainly, I’ll forward ... within the next hour, and note that current line‑up usage is around 78 %..." This answers the request, providing info about capacity utilization (78% usage) and says will forward report. So question answered.

Turn 6: procurement_ally gives benchmark comment, no question.

Turn 7: user asks: "could you indicate whether there is any flexibility to meet or improve on that figure while preserving your margin? Emma, once we receive the data, could you confirm whether a 30‑day lead time remains feasible given the current capacity?" Two questions: one to supplier_ceo about price flexibility, second to Emma (quality_director) about lead time feasibility.

Turn 8: supplier_ceo says "We can meet the 83 RMB unit price and the 30‑day lead time remains feasible". Answers both.

Turn 9: quality_director asks for more specifics in report: "please include ...". That's a request for details, not a direct question but a request. Supplier later provides.

Turn 10: user confirms price and lead time, asks Emma to confirm inspection protocol. That's a request.

Turn 11: supplier_ceo provides capacity report, quality audit, and joint inspection protocol. Good.

Turn 12: quality_director says they are prepared to adopt protocol but want amendment. Not a question.

Turn 13: user confirms price, lead time, accepts protocol with amendment. No question.

Turn 14: supplier_ceo confirms and provides mitigation plan. No question.

Turn 15: quality_director thanks and confirms ability to meet lead time. No question.

Turn 16: user asks: "Please forward the final contract draft ... Additionally, could you confirm the proposed payment schedule ...?" Two requests.

Turn 17: supplier_ceo says will send draft, payment schedule acceptable. Answers.

Turn 18: user thanks and asks to forward payment terms sheet. That's a request, answered later.

Turn 19: supplier_ceo says will email draft and terms sheet. Good.

Turn 20: procurement_ally comments about price. No question.

Turn 21: user asks: "Could you confirm the expected delivery time of those files (e.g., by end of day)?" That's a question.

Turn 22: supplier_ceo says will email by close of business today. Answers.

Turn 23: user: "Let's agree on what we can decide today, then record the unresolved point and who will follow it up." No question.

Turn 24: procurement_ally says only item left is final contract draft, record that Mr. Wang will deliver. No question.

Turn 25: user confirms price etc, asks Mr. Wang to forward docs. That's a request.

Turn 26: procurement_ally repeats price comment.

Turn 27: user asks if need any additional info to finalize docs. That's a question.

Turn 28: supplier_ceo says will forward docs, asks let me know if need additional details. Answers.

Turn 29: procurement_ally repeats price comment.

Turn 30: user asks to forward docs by close of business, let me know if need additional info. Already asked earlier, but it's a request.

Turn 31: supplier_ceo confirms will send by 5pm, asks if need further info. Answers.

Turn 32: user asks to confirm once draft emailed, arrange brief call. That's a request.

Turn 33: supplier_ceo says contract reflects terms, asks for convenient time for call. That's a question.

Turn 34: quality_director asks: "please confirm that final contract draft will incorporate full quality protocol ...". That's a request.

Turn 35: user repeats same request.

Turn 36: supplier_ceo says will make sure draft reflects protocol, will forward.

Turn 37: user confirms price etc, asks to email final draft by 5pm, can we schedule call at 4pm? That's a request.

Turn 38: quality_director confirms capacity etc, will email draft by 5pm, confirms call at 4pm. Answers.

Turn 39: user confirms, looks forward to receiving draft, asks if any additional info needed before call. That's a request.

Turn 40: quality_director says has draft prepared, will email by 5pm, has all info, looks forward to call. Answers.

Turn 41: procurement_ally says no further adjustments needed. No question.

Turn 42: user asks: "please confirm once you have emailed the final contract draft and payment‑terms sheet, and share a brief agenda for our 4 pm call". That's a request.

Turn 43: supplier_ceo proposes agenda. Answers.

Turn 44: quality_director repeats agenda. Answers.

Turn 45: user thanks. No question.

Turn 46: supplier_ceo confirms joint inspection protocol finalized, will be reflected in contract. No question.

Turn 47: quality_director says will have protocol ready for call. No question.

Turn 48: user asks: "could you please let me know as soon as the final contract draft and payment‑terms sheet have been emailed? Also, could you share the brief agenda you outlined so we can circulate it". That's a request.

Turn 49: supplier_ceo says will email and include agenda. Answers.

Turn 50: user thanks.

Turn 51: supplier_ceo confirms joint inspection finalized. No question.

Turn 52: procurement_ally says no remaining open items. No question.

Thus, all questions/requests have been answered or deferred with reasonable timeline. No refusals. No missing answers. Interaction structure fidelity seems maintained.

Potential issues: At turn 5, supplier says "note that current line‑up usage is around 78 % with no material bottlenecks identified that would jeopardize a 30‑day lead time." The earlier request asked for capacity utilization report and quality audit results. Supplier said will forward within next hour, and gave a brief note. That's acceptable.

All handoffs: When user asks Emma to confirm, Emma (quality_director) later does confirm. Good.

Thus classification: "clear" (no violation). Provide rationale.
